phase_0.boundary_condition: The electroweak scale (v ≈ 246 GeV): below this energy the SU(2)×U(1) symmetry is broken and gauge bosons acquire mass through the Higgs mechanism; above it symmetry is restored and all gauge bosons are massless. The boundary is the vacuum expectation value of the Higgs field.

VINIT.justification: Before electroweak symmetry breaking, all four gauge bosons (W¹, W², W³, B) are massless and the full gauge symmetry is unbroken. This is the void from which massive particles will emerge.

TANCH.justification: The vacuum expectation value v ≈ 246 GeV forms the closed boundary containing the entire electroweak sector. Above this energy the symmetry is restored; below it the massive phase is the contained reality.

AFWD.justification: The forward morphism: gauge bosons that couple to the Higgs doublet move forward into the massive regime. The W± and Z acquire mass proportional to their coupling strength; the photon, uncoupled, does not transform.

AREV.chosen_element: photon survival as massless gauge field
AREV.justification: The reverse direction: the photon is the gauge boson that does NOT couple to the Higgs. Under symmetry breaking, it reverses away from mass acquisition and remains exactly massless — the U(1)_EM remnant of the broken symmetry.

CLINK.justification: Composition of gauge eigenstates: the physical Z and photon are linear combinations of W³ and B via the Weinberg angle θ_W. CLINK composes the rotation that produces the mass eigenstates from the gauge eigenstates.

IMSCRIB.justification: The Higgs boson is self-referential: its mass is generated by its own mechanism. The quartic self-coupling λ produces m_H = √(2λ)v. IMSCRIB encodes this identity: the Higgs IS the gate through which it acquires its own mass.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: gauge field decomposition into Higgs-coupled and uncoupled components
FSPLIT.justification: The massless SU(2)×U(1) gauge theory splits into two branches: the T-arm carries the three fields that couple to the Higgs doublet (W¹, W², and the W³/B linear combination that becomes Z), acquiring mass; the F-arm carries the orthogonal combination (the photon) that remains massless.

FFUSE.chosen_element: electroweak symmetry restoration at high energy
FFUSE.justification: Above the electroweak scale, the full SU(2)×U(1) symmetry is restored. All gauge bosons become massless again. The fusion of the massive and massless branches recovers exactly the original massless gauge theory — FFUSE(FSPLIT(x)) = x holds because the broken symmetry is a low-energy phenomenon and the underlying theory is exactly symmetric.

EVALT.chosen_element: spontaneous symmetry breaking via Higgs vacuum expectation value
EVALT.justification: The affirmative branch: the Higgs doublet acquires a nonzero vacuum expectation value, breaking SU(2)×U(1) down to U(1)_EM. Three Goldstone bosons are eaten by the W± and Z, giving them longitudinal polarization and mass. This is the success path — mass generation occurs.

EVALF.justification: The negative branch: the photon direction in gauge space does not couple to the Higgs and sees no symmetry breaking. It remains exactly massless with transverse polarization only. This is not a failure but the necessary complement — a massless photon is required for the theory to be renormalizable.

ENGAGR.justification: A paradice held without resolution: at the electroweak scale itself, both the broken and unbroken descriptions are simultaneously valid. The universe holds both the massive W/Z description and the massless gauge theory description. This is the finite-temperature electroweak crossover where neither phase is pure — both states coexist.

IFIX.chosen_element: irreversible electroweak phase transition in cosmic history
IFIX.justification: The universe crossed the electroweak phase transition once, approximately 10⁻¹² seconds after the Big Bang. This crossing is permanently recorded in the mass spectrum of the gauge bosons and cannot be undone. IFIX marks this as an irreversible cosmological event.
